priorStories.headline: Cuba’s electrical grid collapses nationwide
priorStories.body:
Cuba’s energy ministry said the national electrical grid collapsed, cutting power across the island and affecting about 9 million people.

The country’s power system has been under continuing strain from fuel shortages and deteriorating infrastructure.

priorStories.headline: Nigeria investigates mass deaths in state custody
priorStories.body:
Authorities imposed a 6 p.m. overnight curfew in Minna after protests over mining suspects who died in civil defense custody. Reports placed the number of deaths at 33 to 37; officials said many of the detainees were ages 14 to 18.

President Bola Tinubu ordered an investigation, and the government suspended the Niger State civil defense commandant. Reuters reported that security forces fired live rounds during the protests and that a witness saw a body, but responsibility for that death was not established.

priorStories.headline: Pakistan mosque attack kills at least 21
priorStories.body:
A vehicle bombing and attempted armed assault at a mosque near police offices in Kohat killed at least 21 people and wounded 80, authorities said.

Police officers attending Friday prayers were among the casualties. No group immediately claimed responsibility.

priorStories.headline: UN documents 1,004 sexual-violence cases in Ukraine
priorStories.body:
The UN Human Rights Office documented 1,004 verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence in Ukraine from February 2022 through July 2026. It attributed 89% to Russian authorities and 11% to Ukrainian authorities.

The office cautioned that underreporting and restricted access meant the findings were not comprehensive. It found no discernible accountability measures by Russia; Ukraine had taken preventive steps, but accountability remained limited.

sources.name: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine

priorStories.headline: US expands sanctions on Russia and Iran
priorStories.body:
President Donald Trump signed legislation expanding sanctions and prohibitions targeting Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran.

The law targets Russia’s energy and defense sectors and vessels used to evade sanctions. It also gives the president broader authority to impose tariffs on countries that trade with Russia.

priorStories.headline: US court limits rapid third-country deportations
priorStories.body:
The First Circuit Court of Appeals largely upheld a ruling that found the administration’s rapid third-country deportation policy unlawful.

The court said migrants must receive a meaningful opportunity to raise concerns about persecution or torture before being removed to a country not covered by their immigration proceedings. It reversed one portion of the lower court’s decision on procedural grounds, and an administration appeal is expected.

candidates.summary: Iran executed Hossein Pedaran after the Supreme Court upheld his death sentence for espionage and intelligence cooperation with Israel, the judiciary-run Mizan news agency said. Iranian authorities alleged that he supplied Mossad with information about sensitive military and missile sites in Isfahan for financial gain.
candidates.title: Iran executes man convicted of spying for Israel

candidates.summary: AFP reported that the death toll from the September 18 vehicle bombing and attempted assault at a police compound and mosque in Kohat had risen to 31, citing a police official. Earlier reports had placed the toll at at least 21.
candidates.title: Reported toll in Pakistan police compound attack rises to 31

candidates.summary: China's market regulator opened investigations into Meituan unit Beijing Sankuai Information Technology and several online travel-booking businesses linked to Alibaba, Tongcheng and Tujia over suspected unfair competition violations, state broadcaster CCTV reported. The companies said they were cooperating with regulators.
candidates.title: China investigates online platforms over suspected unfair competition

candidates.summary: Russia's liberal Yabloko party said an election observer lost consciousness as police used force to arrest him at a St. Petersburg polling station during the second day of parliamentary voting. Russian officials did not immediately comment. Separately, election authorities claimed voting systems faced cyberattacks and said the attempts were thwarted; the claims were not independently confirmed.
candidates.title: Russian opposition reports observer arrest as officials claim election cyberattacks

candidates.summary: Denmark and Greenland said a pending security agreement with the United States would preserve the Danish kingdom's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination, contrasting with President Donald Trump's description of permanent U.S. control over the island's security. The agreement's full text had not been released and still required parliamentary action before enforcement, according to Denmark's government.
candidates.title: Denmark and Greenland say pending US security deal preserves sovereignty

candidates.summary: Flames and a large plume of black smoke were documented near Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport after Saudi authorities issued overnight warnings of a potential aerial threat. Reuters imagery showed smoke and flames near apparent fuel tanks, but Saudi officials had not identified the cause or reported casualties. Flight delays and cancellations were reported at the airport.
candidates.title: Fire and smoke reported near Riyadh airport after aerial-threat alerts

candidates.summary: Emperor Naruhito formally opened the 20th Asian Games during a ceremony in Nagoya. The 16-day event includes athletes from 45 countries and regions competing across 43 sports, although some basketball and soccer competitions began before the opening ceremony.
candidates.title: Asian Games formally open in Nagoya

candidates.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked unspecified sites in Riyadh with missiles and drones and an Aramco facility in Yanbu. Reuters documented flames and smoke near fuel tanks by Riyadh's main airport, but Saudi authorities had not confirmed the Houthi claims or identified the cause of the fire.
candidates.title: Houthis claim Riyadh and Yanbu attacks as fire burns near airport

candidates.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkey was prepared to help meet Saudi Arabia's technical military needs in response to Houthi attacks. He cited a trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all three.
candidates.title: Turkey offers military support to Saudi Arabia under defense pact
candidates.geography: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Yemen

candidates.summary: Petrobras said its board approved participation in a Brazilian government subsidy program paying diesel producers 1 real per liter for 30 days, with a possible 30-day extension. The state-controlled company said the subsidy would leave its diesel prices to distributors unchanged because it offsets an equal price adjustment.
candidates.title: Petrobras approves participation in Brazil diesel subsidy

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said he planned to establish a federal “AI Force” and appoint an artificial-intelligence coordinator. He provided no immediate details about the proposed body's structure, powers or formation process, and said the appointment would be announced later.
candidates.title: Trump proposes federal AI Force and coordinator
